clue.text: Trendy city where one avoids a complete soaking

definitions.text: where one avoids a complete soaking

parts.note: hip means fashionable, in the know
Bath is a Roman spa city in Somerset, England

explanation.surface: A fashionable spa town where visitors somehow stay dry.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description: a hip bath is a small tub you sit in, so only your lower half gets wet.
explanation.definitionFit: A hip bath covers only the seated lower body, so the bather never goes fully under the water.

clue.text: One taken with the net, perhaps, using computer — one only

definitions.text: One taken with the net, perhaps

parts.note: HAL is the murderous computer in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey
the Roman numeral for one
but can mean only, as in 'she is but a child'

explanation.surface: Someone surfing the internet on a computer, a lone user caught up in the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The net' tempts you towards the internet, especially next to 'computer'; it is a fishing net, and 'perhaps' flags the definition as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: This large flatfish is commonly landed by trawlers, so it is one example of a catch hauled aboard in nets.

clue.text: Lift, open and restart after repairing

indicators.note: repairing puts broken things back together in a new working order, so the letters are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for an elevator that has broken down: open it and start it again once fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' reads as a verb but is the British noun for an elevator. A paternoster is an old open-fronted lift of doorless cars on a continuous loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A paternoster is a type of elevator whose open compartments circulate continuously, so passengers step on and off while it moves.

clue.text: Ridiculous muscles seen on Murdo when stripped

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles

indicators.note: stripping takes off the outer covering, so only the inner letters of the word stay

parts.note: Murdo, a Scottish first name, without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A man called Murdo strips off and reveals comically impressive muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the muscles sit on top of the stripped name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something so silly or unreasonable that it invites laughter; they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Cleric from school, nuisance about teaching scripture?

parts.note: a high school, a type of secondary school

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a pest is an annoying person
RI is Religious Instruction, the old British school subject

explanation.surface: A clergyman with a schoolroom grievance about a troublesome scripture teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: RI (Religious Instruction) was the name for religious education lessons in British schools; the question mark admits the definition-by-description.
explanation.definitionFit: A high priest is the chief religious official, as in ancient Judaism, so he is a senior member of the clergy.

clue.text: Drop a trail of blood?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fall or downward slope
second meaning: lineage, the bloodline traced back through ancestors

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests drips of blood, but 'blood' here is ancestry, and a trail of blood is the family line you follow back.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a downward fall and a person's ancestry or heritage, the line from parent to child.

clue.text: Curse desperate character overcoming resistance

indicators.note: to overcome is to get over and around an obstacle, so one piece envelops the other

parts.note: Desperate Dan, the strongman cowboy of the British children's comic The Dandy
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A desperate person swears as they finally beat the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperate' looks like an adjective but belongs to a name: Desperate Dan is a famous British comic-strip character.
explanation.definitionFit: Darn is a mild euphemism used as an expletive, so it serves as a gentle swear word.

clue.text: Top professionals turned up carrying Caesar's first ballista

indicators.note: in a down clue, flipping skyward makes the letters read in the opposite direction

parts.note: number one, written NO I

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: pros is short for professionals

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the initial of Caesar

explanation.surface: Elite troops arrive with Julius Caesar's best siege engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' alone gives NO I, number one, which joins PROS before the whole string is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman scorpio or scorpion was a small torsion catapult firing bolts, a type of ballista used by legions.

clue.text: Skin sizeable amphibian

indicators.note: to skin is to remove the outer layer, so the outside letters go

parts.note: sizeable is HEFTY, which loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to skin a large frog or toad.
explanation.walkthrough: Hefty means big and heavy; peel off its outer letters and the creature is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a newt, especially a young one on land, and newts are amphibians.

clue.text: Little 'un beginning to teethe left in care of stranger

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of teethe

indicators.note: being in someone's care means being held within their keeping

parts.note: odder means more strange
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A teething baby left with a babysitter it does not know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' reads as a person, but it is the comparative adjective: more strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A small child who has just learned to walk is a young one, which is what 'little one' affectionately means.

clue.text: Allowed knight to leave fast

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the word

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight is given permission to ride off quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adverb meaning quickly, but it is a noun: a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone do something is to permit it, so the past form matches allowed exactly.

clue.text: Return meat sauces firm had marked at the back "with added sweetener"

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ragus, plural of ragu, the Italian meat sauce
Co is the abbreviation for company
had a meal, so ate

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of marked

explanation.surface: A food firm's labelling of sauces sent back for containing added sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' reads as a verb about sending goods back; it reverses the sauces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coated in a layer of sugar has had extra sweetness put on it, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Henry and Norm snatch back chart

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so everything reads right to left

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
par is the standard or norm
to grab is to snatch

explanation.surface: Two men, Henry and Norm, grab back a map or diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry and Norm look like two people's names; one is a unit of measurement and the other a common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram that shows quantities as rectangles of different lengths is a kind of chart.

clue.text: Turns round large urban area

indicators.note: to bring something round is to swing it to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: warps means twists or bends out of shape
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Directions that swing around a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large urban area' looks like the whole definition, but 'large' supplies a letter and the definition is just the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban sprawl is the spread of housing and roads outward from a city, so the word names that built-up expanse.

clue.text: Venerable Hindu possibly sets aside day devoted to a Christian saint

parts.note: august means respected and impressive

indicators.note: setting something aside puts it out of the way, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a Hindu may well be Indian, 'possibly' marking an example
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A revered Hindu holy man takes a day off to honour a Christian saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venerable' looks like a title, as in the Venerable Bede, but it is simply the adjective august.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustinian describes followers of St Augustine of Hippo, such as the religious order named after him.

clue.text: Caught husband with resin and cannabis in vessel used after dark?

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
H is the abbreviation for husband
amber is fossilised tree resin
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A husband is caught on a night-time boat with drugs and resin aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship carrying contraband; it is a container, and the question mark admits the description is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: Before indoor toilets, people kept a pot under the bed to relieve themselves during the night.

clue.text: Hammer-wielding chap stealing gold from writer

indicators.note: stealing takes something away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Henry David Thoreau, the American author of Walden
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A man with a hammer robbing an author of his gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer's surname ends in the chemical symbol for gold, which is taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse god of thunder carries the hammer Mjolnir, so he is the mythical figure who swings one.

clue.text: Sole trader following me, horsing around

parts.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: fooling around is messing about, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A one-person business owner larking about behind the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole trader' is a business term for a self-employed person, but sole here is the flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sells fish such as sole for a living is a dealer in that kind of produce.

clue.text: Paraffin smoke rose, nearly chokes

indicators.note: to choke on something is to have it caught in the throat, held inside

parts.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: Burning paraffin gives off fumes that rise until someone almost chokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' looks like a deletion signal, but it is only part of the string that holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is the British name for the lamp and heating oil that Americans and Australians call by this other name.

clue.text: Concerning brewing smooth beer

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients into something new, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note about making a smooth-tasting ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concerning' reads as 'about', introducing a topic, but it is the adjective meaning worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worrying or troubling causes anxiety, which is what an irksome or annoying matter does.

clue.text: City diary penned by a toff from the south

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in an enclosure, so one piece sits inside another
in a down clue, reading from the bottom upward runs the letters backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a nob is a posh upper-class person, British slang like toff
a log is a daily record

explanation.surface: A journal written by an aristocrat while travelling up from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is a British word for a posh, upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Bologna is a large historic city in northern Italy, famous for its university and its food.

clue.text: Offshore location one's going to for broadcast

indicators.note: a broadcast is something spoken over the air, so we go by what is heard

parts.note: one's going to do it means I'll do it, said by the speaker

explanation.surface: A radio station that broadcasts from somewhere out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the speaker, so 'one's going to' is the contraction I'll, which sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An island lies off the coast surrounded by water, so it is a place out beyond the shore.

clue.text: Model, former partner, somewhat bulky?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ample means generously sized, a polite word for rather large

explanation.surface: A fashion model whose ex-partner has put on a little weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a catwalk; it is a pattern to copy, and the question mark admits ample is only roughly bulky.
explanation.definitionFit: A model is something to follow or imitate, so a good instance to copy serves as a pattern.

clue.text: Page, upstanding retro hotel employee

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page

indicators.note: standing up in a down clue makes the letters read from the bottom upward

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An honest bellboy at an old-fashioned hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Page' looks like the definition, since a page is a hotel messenger, but it supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A porter carries guests' luggage or staffs the door, one of the standard jobs on a hotel's staff.

clue.text: Young male forward fed a bit of rancid fat

indicators.note: feeding puts something inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: a lad is a boy or young man

indicators.note: a small bit of a word is just its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of rancid
on means forward, as in 'go on'

explanation.surface: A teenage boy being made to eat a piece of rotten fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of rancid fat' wants to be the definition; only 'fat' defines, and 'a bit of' takes one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lardon is a strip or cube of pork fat or bacon used in cooking, so it is a piece of fat.

clue.text: Working on emails — it's part of the grind

indicators.note: working means being processed or reworked, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Answering emails is just part of the daily office grind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The grind' sounds like tedious routine work, but it is literally the grinding of wheat in a mill.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is the coarse particles of durum wheat left from milling, so it is one product of grinding grain.

clue.text: Crack line taken from Dickensian villain

indicators.note: taking something from a whole removes it, so a letter goes

parts.note: Daniel Quilp, the vicious dwarf in The Old Curiosity Shop
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A crack in a line from a Dickens novel's villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' sounds like a split or fracture; it is a wisecrack, a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack in the sense of a wisecrack is a witty remark, which is exactly a short clever joke.

clue.text: Might a children's entertainer have had a hand in this?

definitions.text: Might a children's entertainer have had a hand in this?

parts.words: Might a children's entertainer have had a hand in this?
parts.note: surface reading: was a party entertainer involved in or responsible for something
setter's reading: the entertainer's hand is literally inside the toy, working it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Had a hand in' is an idiom for being involved, but here it is literal: the performer's hand goes inside the figure.
explanation.definitionFit: This toy fits over the hand like a mitten, and children's entertainers work it with their fingers to make it talk.

clue.text: Choose cape shunned by African Christian

indicators.note: being shunned means being kept out, so that letter is left out

parts.note: a Copt is a member of the ancient Christian church of Egypt
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: An African churchgoer refuses to pick a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape' reads as a garment; it is the headland abbreviation found on maps.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to make a selection between alternatives, the same as picking or deciding.

clue.text: Little monkey's spotted leaving river

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so those letters depart from the word

parts.note: spotted in the sense of stained or contaminated
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A small monkey has been seen climbing out of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like 'seen'; it means marked or unclean. The Ure is a short river name crosswords use often.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a naughty child a little monkey means a mischief-maker, which is what this word means.

clue.text: Port wine drained after soldier pair retired

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant

indicators.note: a drained vessel is emptied of its contents, so only the outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of wine

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: pr is the abbreviation for pair

explanation.surface: A bottle of port emptied once two old soldiers had gone to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port wine' looks like one phrase, but 'Port' alone is the definition, a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp in Belgium is one of Europe's biggest seaports, on the River Scheldt.

clue.text: Time before new Anglican dramatist

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
ere is an old word for before
N is the abbreviation for new
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A playwright who came before the new Church of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church of England is the Anglican church, abbreviated CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence was a Roman writer of comedies in the second century BC, so he is a classical playwright.
